implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class defines ROWS = 6 and COLUMNS = 7 and creates a 6x7 grid in __init__.
Game class stores two Player instances, tracks current_index, and switches player after each valid move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: Player.get_move prompts "choose a column (1-7)" and reads input with input().
Game.play calls board.drop_disc to place the disc and then board.display to show the updated board.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four discs
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win examines four directions (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals) using _count_direction.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range and not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_column checks bounds and that the top cell is empty; Player.get_move re‑prompts if invalid.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game when a winning line is detected or the grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.play breaks the loop after board.check_win returns true or board.is_full returns true, then calls announce_result.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graceful handling of EOF / input interruption
implemented_requirements.evidence: Both safe_input in main.py and exception handling in Player.get_move exit cleanly on EOFError or KeyboardInterrupt.

judge.summary: All core Connect Four features are present: a 7×6 board, two alternating players, numeric column input with validation, disc placement with gravity, win detection in all directions, draw detection, and clean termination. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to run.
